newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA eyes retail banking venture in China.
newsitem.headline: CBA eyes retail banking venture in China.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) has discussed with Chinese officials the prospects for a retail banking joint venture in China, CBA Managing Director David Murray said on Wednesday.

Murray told reporters after a luncheon address to the Committee for Economic Development (CEDA) that he had spoken to Chinese officials early this month when he went to China in the joint diplomatic/business delegation led by Prime Minister John Howard. He said the discussions were primarily about extending CBA's current representative office to a full branch, but that the bank was also looking at joint venture prospects.
"Joint ventures would be of interest if we can get involved in the sort of basic banking activities that are part of our core skills here," Murray said.
CBA is Australia's largest home loan lender and has concentrated on retail banking services for individuals rather than corporate or wholesale banking services.
